newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed says Fermi nuke restart delayed.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed says Fermi nuke restart delayed.

text.p: Detroit Edison's 1,116 megawatt Fermi 2 nuclear power unit in Monroe County, Mich., will not restart this weekend as scheduled, the company said Friday.
"They're still working on one of the 15 safety release valves," company spokeswoman Mary Kay Bean said, noting additional work would be carried out next week.
She could not comment on the duration of the work or when the unit would likely restart.
A faulty indicator light, which should indicate when a safety release valve is open, caused the unit to shut last Saturday while restarting from a scheduled outage.
The unit originally shut for maintenance and refueling September 27.
Detroit Edison is a unit of DTE Energy Co.
Forecasters are calling for below-normal temperatures beginning early next week throughout most of the Midwest.
The spokeswoman explained that the remaining work was being carried out in the facility's control room, where the safety release valves' indicator lights are located.
